idea:
GitHub issue #45 on mtgibbs/pi-cluster-mcp: Pi-hole stats are primary-only — the secondary is never polled (HA DNS observability gap).

Pi-hole stats are collected from the primary only. PIHOLE_URL is unset, so it defaults to pihole-web, whose Service selector is app: pihole. The secondary runs as app: pihole-secondary and the client has no secondary support, so it is never polled. On our HA DNS (two Pi-hole instances), stats only reflect one of the two resolvers; queries served by the secondary are invisible, and a secondary-only auth/health problem would not show up in get_dns_status. The brainrot CronJob iterates both hosts explicitly (HOSTS="192.168.1.55 192.168.1.56").

Suggested fix: support a list of Pi-hole hosts (env or config), not a single PIHOLE_URL. Authenticate and fetch stats per instance; aggregate totals and/or surface per-instance health so a single-node failure is visible.

===== specs/pihole-secondary-stats/spec.md =====
# Spec: Pi-hole secondary stats (multi-host polling)

## 1. Why · [R]

`src/clients/pihole.ts` reads a single `PIHOLE_URL` (default `http://pihole-web.pihole.svc.cluster.local`),
whose Service selects `app: pihole`. The secondary Pi-hole runs as `app: pihole-secondary` and the
client has no notion of a second host, so it is never polled: `get_dns_status` reports the stats of
one of the two HA resolvers, queries served by the secondary are invisible, and a secondary-only
auth/health problem never surfaces. The brainrot CronJob already solves this by iterating both
hosts explicitly (`HOSTS="192.168.1.55 192.168.1.56"`); the MCP client should do the same.

## 2. Outcomes · [R]

1. Setting `PIHOLE_URLS` (comma/space separated) makes the client poll **every** listed instance:
   one `POST /api/auth` and one `stats/summary` per instance.
2. With a single host (`PIHOLE_URL` set, or neither var set → `http://pihole-web.pihole.svc.cluster.local`)
   behaviour is exactly as today — same request sequence, same `PiholeFullStats` shape.
3. `getFullStats()` returns **aggregated** totals in the existing top-level fields: `dns_queries_today`
   and `ads_blocked_today` are the sum over instances, `ads_percentage_today` is recomputed from those
   sums, `domains_being_blocked` / `gravity_last_updated` come from the healthiest instance, and
   query-type percentages are recomputed from the summed raw type counts.
4. `getFullStats()` additionally returns a `servers` array with one entry per configured host
   (`url`, `ok`, `queriesToday`, `blockedToday`, `domainsBlocked`, `error?`) so per-instance health is
   visible in a single call.
5. If **some but not all** instances fail, the successful instances are still aggregated and the tool
   reports partial data instead of failing.
6. If **every** instance fails, the aggregate reports nothing: `getFullStats()` throws an `Error`
   whose message names the failing host(s) and carries the first instance error, so `get_dns_status`
   keeps producing `statsError`. A total failure must never be reported as zeroes.
7. Existing auth norms hold per instance: sessions are cached per host and a burst of concurrent
   `getFullStats()` calls performs at most ONE login per host (pi-cluster-mcp#48).

## 3. Entities · [E]

- Env var `PIHOLE_URLS` (new): comma- and/or whitespace-separated list of Pi-hole base URLs.
  Takes precedence over `PIHOLE_URL`; when unset/empty, fall back to `PIHOLE_URL` then
  `http://pihole-web.pihole.svc.cluster.local` (single host).
- `src/clients/pihole.ts` new exports:
  - `interface PiholeServerStats { url: string; ok: boolean; queriesToday?: number; blockedToday?: number; domainsBlocked?: number; error?: string }`
  - `function getPiholeUrls(): string[]` — the parsed, de-duplicated host list.
  - `PiholeFullStats` gains `servers: PiholeServerStats[]`.
  - `updateGravity(targets?: string[]): Promise<string>` — optional explicit host list.
- `src/tools/dns.ts`: `get_dns_status` `result.stats` gains a `servers` field (omitted when only one
  host is configured) and keeps `statsError` semantics; `update_pihole_gravity` is unchanged
  behaviourally (primary only).
- Unchanged: `PIHOLE_API_TOKEN` / `PIHOLE_PASSWORD` (one shared password for all instances),
  `src/tools/index.ts`, auth middleware, `package.json`, `k8s/`.

## 4. Approach · [A]

Turn the module-level singleton into a per-instance session store keyed by base URL: a
`Map<string, { sid, expiry }>`, a per-host `authInFlight` promise and a per-host `rateLimitedUntil`,
while keeping every error message and the cooldown semantics of #44/#48 unchanged (they must stay
attributable to a host). Add `getPiholeUrls()` which parses `PIHOLE_URLS` (split on
`[,\s]+`, trim, drop empties, de-duplicate, strip trailing `/`), falling back to `PIHOLE_URL` then
the current default so single-host deployments see no change. `piholeFetch` takes the base URL as a
parameter; the exported read functions take an optional `url` argument defaulting to
`PIHOLE_URL || default`, so `getSummary`, `getTopItems`, `getMessages`, `getWhitelist`,
`getRecentQueries` keep their current signatures and results for existing callers. `getFullStats()`
fans out over the host list with `Promise.allSettled`, builds `servers`, then aggregates the
fulfilled instances into the existing fields (sums for queries/blocked, recomputed percentage,
recomputed type percentages, primary/first-successful instance for gravity and domains-blocked). A
host that fails auth contributes an `ok: false` entry with the error text and is excluded from the
totals; if none succeed the function throws.

Rejected alternatives: (a) a per-instance `PIHOLE_URL_SECONDARY` env var — hardcodes "two", the
issue asks for a list; (b) a new `get_dns_status` per-instance tool or any new tool registration —
more risk in `src/tools/index.ts` and `auth.ts` for no extra observability; (c) a Kubernetes
Service-scanning discovery step — needs new RBAC reasoning and makes tests non-deterministic;
(d) rewriting the exported signatures of every read function to require a url — churn for callers
(`src/tools/dns.ts`, `src/__tests__/write-tool-gates.test.ts` mocks) with no behaviour change.

## 5. Scope · [S]

In scope:
- `src/clients/pihole.ts` (multi-host config, per-host sessions, `getFullStats` fan-out + aggregation)
- `src/tools/dns.ts` (`get_dns_status` surfaces `stats.servers`; pass the configured list to `updateGravity`)
- `src/__tests__/pihole-secondary.test.ts` (new test file, titles fixed in §11)

Out of scope:
- `k8s/` manifests, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `docs/` (deployment wiring for `PIHOLE_URLS` is a
  follow-up in the pi-cluster repo), `package.json`, CI, `src/tools/index.ts`, `src/auth.ts`,
  `test_dns_query` / `diagnose_dns` pod-selection labels (`app=pihole`), gravity fan-out to secondaries.

## 6. Prior facts · [S]

- `src/clients/pihole.ts:4-5` reads `PIHOLE_URL` / `PIHOLE_API_TOKEN|PIHOLE_PASSWORD` into
  module-level consts at import time; `src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts:43-46` re-imports the
  module after `vi.stubEnv` to exploit that. Any new env parsing must stay import-time (or lazily
  re-read the same way) so fresh-import tests see the stub.
- Session state today is a single `sessionId` / `sessionExpiry` plus module-level `authInFlight` and
  `rateLimitedUntil` (`pihole.ts:8-16`); `login()` never runs concurrently with itself and 429 sets a
  cooldown (`RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MS = 60_000`) so retries fail fast with "suppressed".
- `getSummary()`, `getQueryTypes()`, `getStatus()` all hit `stats/summary` and `getFullStats()`
  (line 470) fans out `getSummary` + `getTopItems` + `getQueryTypes` in parallel — this is the burst
  #48 single-flighted.
- `src/tools/dns.ts:68-101` only fetches stats when a pihole pod is ready, wraps the fetch in
  try/catch and sets `result.statsError` from the error message; `getFullStats` is the only stats
  entry point used by tools (`dns.ts:3,71`).
- `src/tools/dns.ts:182-221` `update_pihole_gravity` has a 5-minute cooldown + in-flight gate and
  calls `updateGravity()` (which hits `POST /api/action/gravity` on `PIHOLE_URL`).
- `src/__tests__/write-tool-gates.test.ts:38-44` mocks the pihole client with `getFullStats`,
  `getMessages`, `getWhitelist`, `getRecentQueries`, `updateGravity` — those exports must keep
  existing signatures.
- CLAUDE.md norms: never `String(obj)` on unknown errors; summary-first responses so small models
  relay a verdict; secrets (the Pi-hole password) must never appear in tool output; read-only tools
  must not gain write abilities; tests use vitest with `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', …)` and fresh imports.

## 7. Norms · [N]

- Error messages name the host they came from and keep the #44/#48 wording for auth failure
  (`PIHOLE_API_TOKEN must equal the Pi-hole web password`) and throttling (`rate-limit` /
  `suppressed`, never blaming the credential) — per host, so a single bad secondary is obvious.
- Per-instance error text in `servers[].error` is the message only: no passwords, no request bodies,
  no `String(obj)` on unknown values (`err instanceof Error ? err.message : JSON.stringify(err)`).
- Tests: new file `src/__tests__/pihole-secondary.test.ts`, vitest, `vi.stubEnv` in `beforeEach`,
  `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn(...))`, fresh import via `vi.resetModules()` like `pihole-auth.test.ts`.
- Keep `explicit-function-return-type` clean and no `any` (ESLint config).

## 8. Safeguards · [S]

- No secret may appear in any tool output or log line: the Pi-hole password is never echoed, and
  `servers[].url` is the base URL only (no userinfo, no query string).
- No tool gains a write: `get_dns_status` stays `readOnly: true`; the secondary must NOT start
  receiving `POST /api/action/gravity` — `update_pihole_gravity` keeps targeting the primary list
  only (gravity fan-out is a separate decision).
- No fail-open: if every instance errors, `getFullStats()` must throw rather than return zeros or an
  empty `servers` array, so `get_dns_status` still reports `statsError`.
- Backwards compatible: unset `PIHOLE_URLS` ⇒ exactly one host and byte-compatible response shape
  (only additive `servers`), existing `pihole-auth.test.ts` titles must still pass unchanged.
- No new dependencies, no new env vars besides `PIHOLE_URLS`, no network calls at import time.

## 9. Tasks · [O]

- T1: Add `PIHOLE_URLS` parsing (`getPiholeUrls()`), per-host session/auth state, and url-parameterised
  fetches in `src/clients/pihole.ts`.
- T2: Make `getFullStats()` fan out across all instances, add `PiholeServerStats` + `servers`, aggregate
  totals, and throw when every instance fails; let `updateGravity()` accept an explicit target list.
- T3: Surface `stats.servers` from `get_dns_status` in `src/tools/dns.ts` (multi-host only) without
  changing `statsError` semantics or any tool's read/write flag.
- T4: Add `src/__tests__/pihole-secondary.test.ts` with the six test titles named in §11.
- T5: Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and fix any fallout in the
  files above only.

## 10. Acceptance criteria (EARS) · [O]

1. When `PIHOLE_URLS` lists two hosts, the system shall issue one `/api/auth` and one `stats/summary`
   request per host, using each host's own base URL.
2. When `PIHOLE_URLS` lists two hosts, `getFullStats()` shall return `dns_queries_today` and
   `ads_blocked_today` equal to the sum over the instances, and `ads_percentage_today` recomputed from
   those sums.
3. If a configured instance fails (auth, HTTP, or network), then the system shall include it in
   `servers` with `ok: false` and a non-empty `error`, and shall aggregate the remaining instances.
4. If every configured instance fails, then `getFullStats()` shall reject with an error naming the
   failing host(s), and shall not return aggregated zeros.
5. When only `PIHOLE_URL` is set, the system shall poll exactly that one host and shall not emit a
   `servers` field from `get_dns_status`.
6. When concurrent `getFullStats()` calls overlap, the system shall perform at most one login per host.
7. When `PIHOLE_URLS` is set to two hosts, `get_dns_status`'s `stats` object shall contain a
   `servers` array with one entry per host.

## 11. Verification

`verify.sh` runs offline (mocked `fetch` inside vitest) and asserts:

- **C1** `getPiholeUrls` is exported from `src/clients/pihole.ts` (greps the export) and the string
  `PIHOLE_URLS` appears in the client. Fails today: neither exists — proof multi-host config was added.
- **C2** `PiholeServerStats` is exported from `src/clients/pihole.ts`. Fails today: no per-instance type.
- **C3** `src/tools/dns.ts` references `servers` (grep). Fails today: `get_dns_status` builds no such field.
- **C4** the new test file `src/__tests__/pihole-secondary.test.ts` exists and contains the exact titles:
  - `it('polls every host in PIHOLE_URLS and aggregates their totals', …)`
  - `it('marks a failing instance ok:false and still aggregates the healthy one', …)`
  - `it('throws rather than reporting zeros when every instance fails', …)`
  - `it('falls back to a single host when PIHOLE_URLS is unset', …)`
  - `it('logs in at most once per host for concurrent getFullStats calls', …)`
  Fails today: the file does not exist.
- **C5** `npx vitest run src/__tests__/pihole-secondary.test.ts` passes — the behavioural check for
  outcomes 1–6 (per-host requests, sums, recomputed percentages, partial failure, total failure,
  single-host fallback, single login per host). Fails if any of those behaviours is missing or wrong.
- **C6** `npx vitest run src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts` still passes — guards against regressing
  the #44/#48 auth norms (session header, single-flight, 429 wording, unauthenticated deployment).

## 12. Open questions

- Should `PIHOLE_URLS` be surfaced in `k8s/deployment.yaml`/`CLAUDE.md` as part of this change? Left
  out to keep the PR to `src/`; deployment wiring belongs in the pi-cluster repo.
- Should gravity updates fan out to secondaries? Deliberately not done here (§8): it is a write with
  a 5-minute cooldown and deserves its own decision.
- Are the two instances' `unique_domains` / `unique_clients` comparable? They are not summable
  (same client on both), so the aggregate keeps the primary/first-healthy instance's value rather
  than inventing a sum.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Gate for spec: pihole-secondary-stats (pi-cluster-mcp#45)
# Offline + deterministic: the new tests mock global fetch, so no network or cluster is touched.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

CLIENT=src/clients/pihole.ts
TOOL=src/tools/dns.ts
TEST=src/__tests__/pihole-secondary.test.ts

PASS=0
FAIL=0

check() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "PASS: $name"
    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
  else
    echo "FAIL: $name"
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
  fi
}

file_has() { grep -Eq -- "$2" "$1"; }

# --- C1: multi-host config exists in the client -------------------------------------------
check "C1a PIHOLE_URLS env var is read by $CLIENT" file_has "$CLIENT" 'PIHOLE_URLS'
check "C1b getPiholeUrls is exported from $CLIENT" \
  grep -Eq 'export (async )?function getPiholeUrls|export \{[^}]*getPiholeUrls|export const getPiholeUrls' "$CLIENT"

# --- C2: per-instance health type ----------------------------------------------------------
check "C2 PiholeServerStats type is exported from $CLIENT" \
  grep -Eq 'export (interface|type) PiholeServerStats' "$CLIENT"

# --- C3: the tool surfaces per-instance health ---------------------------------------------
check "C3 $TOOL surfaces a servers field in get_dns_status stats" file_has "$TOOL" 'servers'

# --- C4: the new test file exists with the exact required titles ---------------------------
check "C4a $TEST exists" test -f "$TEST"
check "C4b test 'polls every host in PIHOLE_URLS and aggregates their totals'" \
  grep -Eq "it\(\s*'polls every host in PIHOLE_URLS and aggregates their totals'" "$TEST"
check "C4c test 'marks a failing instance ok:false and still aggregates the healthy one'" \
  grep -Eq "it\(\s*'marks a failing instance ok:false and still aggregates the healthy one'" "$TEST"
check "C4d test 'throws rather than reporting zeros when every instance fails'" \
  grep -Eq "it\(\s*'throws rather than reporting zeros when every instance fails'" "$TEST"
check "C4e test 'falls back to a single host when PIHOLE_URLS is unset'" \
  grep -Eq "it\(\s*'falls back to a single host when PIHOLE_URLS is unset'" "$TEST"
check "C4f test 'logs in at most once per host for concurrent getFullStats calls'" \
  grep -Eq "it\(\s*'logs in at most once per host for concurrent getFullStats calls'" "$TEST"

# --- C5: behaviour of the new code ---------------------------------------------------------
if npx vitest run "$TEST" >/tmp/pihole-secondary-vitest.log 2>&1; then
  echo "PASS: C5 npx vitest run $TEST"
  PASS=$((PASS + 1))
else
  echo "FAIL: C5 npx vitest run $TEST (see /tmp/pihole-secondary-vitest.log)"
  tail -n 30 /tmp/pihole-secondary-vitest.log
  FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
fi

# --- C6: the #44/#48 auth norms must not regress -------------------------------------------
if npx vitest run src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts >/tmp/pihole-auth-vitest.log 2>&1; then
  echo "PASS: C6 npx vitest run src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts"
  PASS=$((PASS + 1))
else
  echo "FAIL: C6 npx vitest run src/__tests__/pihole-auth.test.ts (see /tmp/pihole-auth-vitest.log)"
  tail -n 30 /tmp/pihole-auth-vitest.log
  FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
fi

echo "verify.sh: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]
